quotedTweet.text:
you can read about and study markets all ur life, only to realize a handful of maxims carry 99% of the load (applies for any field)

the first 20 I could think of:

1. "markets move to cause the maximum amount of pain to the maximum number of people"

2. "markets can handle bad news, they can't handle uncertainty"

3. "cut ur losses fast + let your winners run"

4. "losers average losers"

5. "it was never my buying that made me the $, it was the waiting / "men who can sit tight and be right are uncommon" (livermore)

6. "drawdowns damage your mental capital far more than your financial capital"

7. "show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome"

8. "I hate that comment, 'the market is wrong here.' The market is never wrong. When you own a stock that you think is worth X and is trading half of X, you're wrong. Something is missing. You find out later what it was. The market is always right and it tells you it is right." (effron)

9. "someone knows something / the game is rigged, but always rigged to the upside"

10. "there's a lot more money in optimism than in pessimism"

11. "no one is more bearish than a sold-out bull"

12. "the market is a mirror / if you don't know who u are, the market is an expensive place to find out"

13. "you cant control the market, the only thing you can control is your risk"

14. "your first cut is your best cut / if you're going to panic, panic first"

15. "there are old traders, and there are bold traders, but there are no old bold traders"

16. "if u had a punchcard with 20 holes, and each investment in ur life u had to punch one hole, you'd approach investing differently" (buffett)

17. "investing is a balance of arrogance and humilty" (klarman)

18. "liquidity is a coward that's never there when you need it" (burbank)

19. "any man who is a bear on the future of the America will go broke." JP Morgan

20. and from an old boss: "picking bottoms only gets you one thing...stinky fingers."
